clue.text: Say what you will, the orator isn't paid if he does

definitions.meaning: to talk without restraint, voicing whatever you like

definitions.text: the orator isn't paid if he does
definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a speaker who works for no fee delivers his talk free of charge

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: someone who speaks 'free' is giving the speech gratis.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying whatever you wish without restraint is the idiom's ordinary meaning, and the pun on free of charge covers the unpaid speaker.

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the following word may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Security guards perhaps carry out rescues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RESCUES; 'effecting' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard something is to make it safe, which is one sense of the verb secure.

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for hack is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to hack is to chop, as with an axe
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming hack journalist is writing for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns AXE into EXA; 'papers' looks like newspapers but means examination papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Examination papers are the question sheets of tests, so papers stands for tests sat by students.

parts.note: King's is a college of Cambridge (and of London)
the head is the principal of a school or college

explanation.surface: A pub that is the favourite haunt of a college principal.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name; the head of King's College would be a 'King's head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Many British inns bear this sign showing a monarch, so it names a familiar type of pub.

indicators.note: hold means the word for staff contains the next piece within it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A team of staff hold a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or way, which is one sense of course.

clue.text: High ground obtains early advantage in battle

indicators.note: the high ground gets the advantage placed early, so that word comes in front

parts.note: an edge is an advantage, as in having the edge
a hill is high ground

explanation.surface: An army taking the high ground gains an early advantage in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: EDGEHILL (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War, fought in Warwickshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This Warwickshire ridge gave its name to the opening pitched fight of the English Civil War, an example of a battle.

clue.text: Long to reach agreement on service

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, an expression of agreement
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone longs for an agreement over their service.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Succeed in getting a woman to take it on

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in persuading a woman to take on a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means to follow an heir into an estate or title, not to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title or estate is to receive it as heir, the sense meant here.

parts.note: a vehicle hanging from a wire rope that carries passengers up mountains

explanation.definitionFit: Gondolas hung from a wire rope carry passengers up slopes, matching suspended uphill travel.

clue.text: There are strong links between its members

definitions.text: There are strong links between its members

parts.words: There are strong links between its members
parts.note: sounds like a close-knit team, but means convicts literally joined by fetters

explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners in such a work party are shackled together, so its members are linked by metal fetters.

parts.note: the wash is a batch of laundry

explanation.surface: A laundry room is flooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awash is covered with water, the same as flooded.

clue.text: Is among those left to fight

indicators.note: among means the first word sits inside the phrase for those remaining

parts.note: the rest are those left over

explanation.surface: He is among those who stayed behind to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or oppose, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: in means the word for name goes inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A name listed in the credits as the writer of a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond CHANDLER wrote hard-boiled detective thrillers such as The Big Sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote crime novels featuring Philip Marlowe, an example of a thriller-writer.

definitions.meaning: goes up a wall or mountain
weighing machines, with pans held level

explanation.surface: Someone climbs and keeps their balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for going up a cliff and a noun for weighing instruments.

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
being in credit means having money to spare

explanation.surface: Acknowledging that Bill is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to recognise officially, as with an approved body.

clue.text: Get over unkind act, that's plain to see

parts.note: to clear an obstacle is to get over it
a cut is a hurtful snub

explanation.surface: Getting over someone's unkindness is obviously the thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is sharply defined and obvious, so plain to see.

indicators.note: limits means the word for cut encloses the next word

parts.note: to lance is to cut open
low means poor or inadequate

explanation.surface: A cut limits an already inadequate grant.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a sum of money given regularly, a kind of grant.

clue.text: A Ford not involved in repeated journeys between places

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Ford car not involved in repeated trips between places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' is part of the fodder, not a negative; 'involved' rearranges A FORD NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back and forth between two points is the idiom's plain meaning.

clue.text: Not usually the best of the entries

definitions.text: Not usually the best of the entries

parts.words: Not usually the best of the entries
parts.note: sounds like the weakest competitors, but means a rear door, rarely the grandest way into a house

explanation.definitionFit: A rear door is a way in, an entry, and usually less impressive than the front one.

definitions.meaning: a type of long crusty loaf with diagonal slashes on top

explanation.surface: A baker makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf of white bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a blunder and a kind of loaf baked in Britain.

parts.note: sounds like a weaver, but the cloth is the clergy as a body

explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' means the clergy, as in 'a man of the cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are known collectively as the cloth, so someone serving in it is a churchman.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter the Church, subject to purification

indicators.note: to enter means the next word goes inside the abbreviation for the Church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to join the Church is subject to purification.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make clean, which is to subject something to purification.

indicators.note: transferred means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A debit entry was moved on instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obedient does as told, which is following orders.

parts.note: a conception is an idea
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many

explanation.surface: A theological reference to the Immaculate Conception.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Immaculate Conception; L for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, flawless, which is one sense of immaculate.

parts.note: to swat is to hit
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by an explosion needs bandaging.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in strips of cloth, as one would bandage a wound.

definitions.meaning: to narrow or diminish bit by bit
a slender candle or wick used for lighting

explanation.surface: Dimming the lights gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for diminishing gradually and a noun for a thin candle.

clue.text: When found out, Eddy changed colour

indicators.note: found out suggests the name is exposed and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eddy blushed when he was caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' rearranges EDDY; 'changed colour' looks like a blush but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed describes something whose colour has been altered with a stain or tint.

parts.note: main means principal or major

explanation.surface: A major eastern American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of New England, an example of a US state.

clue.text: There's worse to come out of this

definitions.text: There's worse to come out of this

parts.words: There's worse to come out of this
parts.note: alludes to the saying about leaving one bad situation only to land in a worse one, the fire

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'out of the ___ into the fire' names this cooking vessel as the lesser trouble.

clue.text: Dolly confused English Saint and Welsh Wizard

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the name are muddled

parts.note: St George is the patron saint of England

explanation.surface: Dolly mixes up England's patron saint and a famous Welsh politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges DOLLY; the Welsh Wizard was the nickname of David Lloyd George, Liberal Prime Minister 1916-22.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh-born Prime Minister was nicknamed the Welsh Wizard for his oratory and political skill.
